primary_application_assessments.exact_premise: Poincaré–Lelong: for a nonzero holomorphic function g, with dd^c=(i/(2π))∂bar∂, one has dd^c log|g|²=[div(g)]. For a holomorphic section of a smoothly metrized line bundle, the corresponding formula subtracts the metric curvature.
primary_application_assessments.application: Apply Poincare--Lelong with dd^c=i/(2pi) partial-barpartial to log|s|^2; this gives [H]-kappa. The projective radial density 2(1-x) integrates log x to -3/2, so the full decreasing series is genuinely L1 and its exact closed current is S-A*kappa.

primary_application_assessments.exact_premise: Gauduchon’s metric theorem: on every connected compact complex manifold of complex dimension m≥2, every Hermitian metric is conformal to a smooth positive metric η satisfying dd^c(η^(m−1))=0. In particular, every compact complex surface admits smooth η>0 with dd^cη=0.
primary_application_assessments.application: Use Gauduchon Theorem 2, not the even-Betti Theorem 1. Every specified compact modification is a surface. Its smooth positive dd^c-closed eta gives a finite trace and strictly positive int_E eta; distributional Stokes and subtraction yield C_E*A_K for every tail. No projectivity or pointwise restriction to E is assumed.

primary_application_assessments.exact_premise: Siu decomposition: a closed positive (1,1)-current has a unique weakly convergent divisorial part Σλ_j[D_j], with λ_j the generic current coefficients and positive closed residual current. Every finite partial divisorial sum can be subtracted while retaining positivity; their increasing limit can also be subtracted. Along a prime divisor D, the restriction of the current is λ_D[D].
primary_application_assessments.application: The closed current C*kappa+dd^c q admits subtraction of each finite partial divisorial sum. Their increasing positive-current limit leaves a positive residual. The same argument applies to every w ordinarily equivalent to u; it establishes the residual h without a global dd^c lemma.

primary_application_assessments.exact_premise: On a coordinate domain, a real distribution with positive complex Hessian has a unique locally integrable psh representative. A locally uniformly upper-bounded family of psh functions has a psh usc supremum equal to its pointwise supremum almost everywhere; Choquet’s lemma supplies a countable subfamily with the same usc supremum. These assertions apply to a common smooth closed background after adding local smooth potentials.
primary_application_assessments.application: Work locally in a smooth potential for C*kappa. Choquet finite maxima explicitly include u, so the canonical sequence is between genuine u and zero. Its pullbacks converge almost everywhere off the exceptional locus and in local L1 by domination. Canonical representatives extend the residual inequalities through common poles.

primary_application_assessments.exact_premise: If closed positive currents T_j converge weakly to T on a coordinate domain, their point Lelong numbers satisfy ν(T,x)≥limsup_j ν(T_j,x). For a common quasi-psh background, the corresponding assertion follows after a fixed local smooth correction.
primary_application_assessments.application: For each fixed divisor choose a point outside the countably many nongeneric loci of the sequence and the limit; point Lelong upper semicontinuity then gives the generic lower inequality. The order q>=u gives the reverse inequality. Equivalently, positive subtraction of the fixed coefficient along E persists under the weak-current limit.

primary_application_assessments.exact_premise: Darvas–Xia, Theorem 2.13 and Proposition 2.30: on a compact Kähler manifold, for quasi-psh potentials in a common smooth closed pseudoeffective background, equality of multiplier ideals at every positive real weight is equivalent to equality of point Lelong numbers on every smooth projective modification, and equivalently to equality of all generic divisorial Lelong numbers on those modifications. A point Lelong number equals the generic number on the exceptional divisor of its blowup. Their multiplier-ideal weight is exp(−tφ).
primary_application_assessments.application: Apply Darvas--Xia only in the common sufficiently positive CLOSED C*kappa background on Kahler P2. Equality on all modifications in the hypothesis includes every projective modification and every subsequent point blowup, hence supplies all required point Lelong numbers. The source log-norm normalization is twice the present log-squared divisor coefficient, which leaves equality unchanged.

primary_application_assessments.exact_premise: Demailly’s local Bergman approximation: for psh φ on a bounded pseudoconvex domain and every real m>0, the holomorphic Hilbert space with weight exp(−2mφ) gives φ_m=(2m)⁻¹logΣ|g_m,ℓ|² satisfying φ_m≥φ−C/m. Locally, its singularity and divisorial orders are those of a finite subcollection of the Bergman terms. Every such term belongs locally to the multiplier ideal for weight exp(−2mφ).
primary_application_assessments.application: Use the actual real Bergman parameter m=k/2, not an integer-only approximation. Each Hilbert term has weight exp(-k phi) and lies in the original multiplier ideal. Finite extraction identifies the Bergman subideal order; the full ideal order is no larger. Keeping the Jacobian order j_E in the radial integral gives b-(j_E+1)/k <= e_k/k <= b on each given compact modification.

primary_application_assessments.exact_premise: Bedford–Taylor theory: locally bounded psh potentials have positive closed mixed Hessian products, symmetric and multilinear and continuous under decreasing bounded approximation. On a strongly pseudoconvex coordinate domain, pluripolar sets have zero Bedford–Taylor outer capacity. Consequently bounded local psh mixed products, including trace measures obtained by wedging with a smooth strictly positive local factor, charge no pluripolar set.
primary_application_assessments.application: Bounded local residual potentials yield closed BT products. Their trace measures charge no pluripolar sets by outer capacity nullity, so the countable divisor union is invisible to the residual K. This also justifies the elementary bounded closed BMP bound; BMP is not used to infer a positive lower mass.

primary_application_assessments.exact_premise: BEGZ, Propositions 1.4 and 1.6: non-pluripolar products of closed positive (1,1)-currents are positive, symmetric, multilinear and plurifinely local wherever defined; on compact Kähler manifolds they are defined and have finite mass. They charge no pluripolar sets. For degree one and local potential p, the product is the restriction of the current to {p>−∞}.
primary_application_assessments.application: Use closed finite non-pluripolar products only on Kahler P2. The needed multilinearity follows by bounded multilinearity on intersections of finite strict superlevels and exhaustion of the finite locus; omitted pole sets are pluripolar. Proposition 1.4(c) leaves its proof to the reader, so no nonexistent printed proof is credited. Degree one is exactly K, and positive multilinearity gives the top-mass lower bound (C-A)^2.

primary_application_assessments.exact_premise: Witt Nyström’s closed mass monotonicity: on a compact Kähler manifold, for a fixed smooth closed real (1,1)-background β and genuine β-psh potentials φ,ψ, the inequality φ≥ψ+O(1) implies ∫⟨(β+dd^cφ)^n⟩≥∫⟨(β+dd^cψ)^n⟩. No small-unbounded-locus hypothesis is required.
primary_application_assessments.application: Closed top-mass monotonicity compares u to finite partial sums and compares every w~u in BOTH ordinary-order directions, always with the same closed C*kappa background. In the product proof the ordinary wedge coefficient binomial(n+N,N) must be retained on both sides; it cancels. The probability kernels N*t^(N-1) concentrate at 1 and the closed mixed mass is a finite continuous polynomial in t. No source formula omitting that common factor is imported.

primary_application_assessments.exact_premise: Boucksom–Guedj–Lu’s bounded-background product construction: for bounded quasi-psh potentials and smooth real (1,1)-forms, smooth-background-corrected Bedford–Taylor mixed products are symmetric, multilinear, plurifinely local, non-pluripolar and depend only on the represented currents. The mixed product is positive when all represented currents are positive. The same construction restricts consistently to sets on which the potentials are bounded.
primary_application_assessments.application: Use BGL bounded corrected products only at the SAME max(w,-j) levels in theta and C*kappa, restricted to {w>-j}. Closed degree-two and degree-one products have finite limits. Smooth L=C*kappa-theta preserves convergence of the finite correction measures, and L^2 charges no poles. With dd^c L=0, distributional Stokes computes the actual mass throughout the entire ordinary type.

primary_application_assessments.exact_premise: BFJ, Theorem A: for psh germs u,v at the origin in C^n, equality of point Lelong numbers on every proper modification above the origin is equivalent to equality J+(tu)=J+(tv) for every t>0, where J(u) consists of germs g with |g|²exp(−2u) locally integrable and J+(u) is the stabilized ideal J((1+ε)u) as ε decreases to zero.
primary_application_assessments.application: BFJ Theorem A is originally about J_+ for exp(-2t phi), not directly the current exp(-t phi) notation. Its local theorem is an identified imported foundation of the Darvas--Xia characterization, with its complete theorem and conventions checked. The global characterization needed here is supplied by Darvas--Xia; this audit does not manufacture a local-to-global proof for arbitrary analytic modifications.

primary_application_assessments.exact_premise: Strong openness: for a psh germ φ, with I(φ) defined by local integrability of |g|²exp(−φ), one has I(φ)=⋃_{ε>0}I((1+ε)φ). The same equality applies to quasi-psh germs because smooth additions do not change local integrability.
primary_application_assessments.application: Guan--Zhou Theorem 1.1 applies after a local smooth psh correction and a constant shift to a negative psh weight. For each locally integrable germ it gives p>1 on a smaller polydisc. Coherence and finitely many stalk generators give a common epsilon, hence J_+=J. Smooth bounded additions preserve integrability; t/2 supplies BFJ-to-present normalization for every real t>0.

primary_application_assessments.exact_premise: BEGZ, Theorem 1.16: on a compact Kähler manifold, for cohomologous tuples of closed positive (1,1)-currents T_j,T'_j with small unbounded locus, if every T_j is less singular than T'_j, the difference of the cohomology classes of their non-pluripolar mixed products is pseudoeffective. For top-degree products this implies the corresponding inequality of total masses.
primary_application_assessments.application: BEGZ Theorem 1.16 requires small unbounded locus and cohomologous CLOSED positive currents on a compact Kahler manifold. Those hypotheses hold for the two auxiliary currents on P2 times P^N in Witt Nystrom's construction; they are not imposed incorrectly on the original countable-divisor potential. For top degree pseudo-effectivity is exactly the required nonnegative total-mass difference. The actual theorem and full Stokes/truncation comparison context were read.

strong_openness_actual_context_version: Published Annals 2015 theorem; not a claim to have read every page of the arXiv URL returned by the reviewer.
